page.answer: Short answer. The best 24V 100Ah LiFePO4 battery for the money is the Dyness 24V 100Ah: $0.137 per Wh, low-temperature charge protection, a 5-year warranty and 2,700 Wh measured. If you need to charge below freezing, the heated Epoch 24V 100Ah is $0.468 per Wh, and Epoch's store listed it as sold out on 2026-11-10.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Cost per Wh. Dyness: $349.99 ÷ 2,560 Wh = $0.137. LiTime Bluetooth: $499.99 ÷ 2,560 = $0.195. Epoch Heated: $1,199 ÷ 2,560 = $0.468. Dyness also sells a Bluetooth version at $369.99 ÷ 2,560 = $0.145.
  • Measured against rated. Michael Barton of techtest.org measured the Dyness over three cycles at a constant 20 A. It averaged 2,700.56 Wh, and 2,700.56 ÷ 2,560 = 105.5% of its rating. That works out to $349.99 ÷ 2,700.56 = $0.130 per delivered Wh. The discharge curve he shows ends after about 5 h 17 min at that roughly 512 W load.
  • Inverter size. A 100 A BMS allows 100 × 25.6 V = 2,560 W. A 3,000 W inverter at full load draws 3,000 ÷ 25.6 = 117 A even before inverter losses, which is more than any 100 A pack here can supply. Epoch's 120 A gives 120 × 25.6 = 3,072 W.
  • Rated lifetime. Dyness and LiTime both claim 4,000+ cycles at 100% depth of discharge. 4,000 × 2.56 kWh = 10,240 kWh, so the Dyness costs $349.99 ÷ 10,240 = $0.034 per lifetime kWh and the LiTime $499.99 ÷ 10,240 = $0.049. Both figures rest on the makers' claims; nobody has measured them.

We have no affiliate link for Dyness, so its link goes to Dyness's own store. On the ComFlex, LiTime claims native compatibility only with Victron. Victron's battery compatibility index doesn't list LiTime, and Victron's GX manual says not to enable DVCC unless your battery's notes mention it. That means the inverter-charger won't take its charge limits from this battery's BMS.

Heated or cutoff: what charging below freezing costs

LiFePO4 cells shouldn't be charged below 32°F (0°C); Epoch's spec, for one, lists cell charging from 0°C. A cutoff only refuses the charge. The Dyness stops charging below 32°F and resumes above 41°F, and in a cold RV bay it sits uncharged until it warms up. A heater uses charger current to warm the cells first. The Epoch 24V 100Ah Heated is the heated pack priced here: its heater runs on incoming charge current, and the pack charges from -4°F. Epoch's store listed it as sold out on 2026-11-10, at $0.468 per Wh. Its 11-year warranty gives free replacement in years 1–3, then 40% off MSRP in years 4–11.

Not recommended

LiTime 24V 100Ah (non-Bluetooth), $639.86. That's $639.86 ÷ 2,560 = $0.250 per Wh. Its listing gives a 32–122°F charge range with no cutoff, yet LiTime's own Bluetooth version adds the 32°F cutoff and the app for $639.86 − $499.99 = $139.87 less.
